Basics of DevOps

YAML — A beginners’ guide

Your Devops Buddy
3 min read
·
Sep 11, 2022

What Is It and How Does It Work?

YAML is a simple, user-friendly data serialisation language that works well with various programming languages in real-world applications.

A few examples of typical YAML use cases include configuration files, log files, files for cross-language collaboration, and data sharing. The majority of DevOps technologies, such as Docker, Kubernetes, and even ansible prefer YAML as their configuration language. It is designed to be user-friendly and compatible with other programming languages.

YAML File Rules

Keep the following basic rules in mind when creating a YAML file.

  • YAML has case-sensitive formatting
  • File extensions must be .yaml or .yml
  • When creating YAML files, YAML does not allow the use of tabs; instead, spaces are allowed.

Elements of YAML

List

A list is a collection of elements. Each element of a list is indented and starts with a space.

All members of a list are lines beginning at the same indentation level starting with a "- " (a dash and a space):

---
# A list of books
- The Hobbit
- Game of Thrones
- Lord of Rings
- Sherlock Holmes
...

Dictionary

Dictionaries are groups of key:value mappings. Every key is case-sensitive. It is important to note that a space after the colon is required.

A dictionary is represented in a simple key: value form (the colon must be followed by a space):

# An employee record
Narendra:
  name: Narendra Reddy
  job: Sr. DevOps Engineer
  skill: YAML

Using dictionaries and lists together can create more complex structures:As needed, dictionaries can be nested in lists, and lists can be nested in dictionaries.

# Students records
- Omkar:   # Is a list
    name: Omkar Reddy  # Is a dictionary
    Class: 9.      # is a dictionary
    Subjects:
      - Mathematics
      - Physics
      - English

More complex data structures are possible, such as lists of dictionaries, dictionaries with list values, or a combination of the two:

# Employee records
- Narendra:
    name: Narendra Reddy
    job: Sr. DevOps Engineer
    skills:
      - Kubernetes
      - Docker
      - ANsible
- Krishna:
    name: Krishna Reddy
    job: Program Director
    skills:
      - Salesforce
      - CompTIA A
      - .NET

If you really want to, dictionaries and lists can also be represented in expanded form:

martin: {name: Martin D'vloper, job: Developer, skill: Elite}
fruits: ['Apple', 'Orange', 'Strawberry', 'Mango']

you can also specify a boolean value (true/false) in several ways:

create_key: yes
needs_agent: no
knows_oop: True
likes_emacs: TRUE
uses_cvs: false

Values can be stretched to multiple lines by using either a “literal block scalar”| or a “folded block scalar” >. A “literal block scalar” includes newlines and any trailing spaces. A “folded block scalar” folds newlines into spaces, making what would otherwise be a long line more manageable.Here are some examples:

include_newlines: |
            exactly as you see
            will appear these three
            lines of poetryfold_newlines: >
            this is really a
            single line of text
            despite appearances

There are two ways to enforce a newline to be kept:

fold_some_newlines: >
    africa
    britain    california
    delhi
      Europe
    france

It can also be enforced by including newline n characters:

fold_same_newlines: "a b\nc d\n  e\nf\n"

Let’s put everything we’ve learned so far into practise with a random YAML example.

---
# An employee record
name: Martin D'vloper
job: Developer
skill: Elite
employed: True
foods:
  - Apple
  - Orange
  - Strawberry
  - Mango
languages:
  perl: Elite
  python: Elite
  pascal: Lame
education: |
  4 GCSEs
  3 A-Levels
  BSc in the Internet of Things
